messages.subject: Running biogeobears on multiple trees
parts:
Hi Nick,

I have used a starting tree in BEAST to , and  eventually I ran BioGeoBEARS on the maximum clade credibility tree.
My question is do you think I need to run the model across multiple trees again?  If yes can i do it for 10 trees randomly sampled acorss the posterior since i dont have acess to much powerful computers here. ( I used a starting tree prior assuming that there wont be much topological uncertainties ). Do you think this approach is correct?

Looking forward to hearing form you.

Regards,
Sandy

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Running biogeobears on multiple trees
parts:
Hi!  Like anything, it's a cost-benefit calculation: what do you get from the extra work involved?

My basic thought is: don't do a multiple-trees run "just because" or because of some abstract sense of nervousness or "other people do it" or "more is always better in papers" or "some reviewer might suggest I do multiple trees just-because or because-other-people-do-it or whatever".

*If* you have substantial tree uncertainty and *if* its in a region of the tree where it might effect some important biogeographical inference, then sure, do it.  If (as is common) you're just going to smush all the individual tree biogeography analyses back onto some summary tree anyway, then I don't see too much point.

I've posted some further thoughts at:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/biogeobears/M8zw8Kidseo

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/biogeobears/kASdtlF2bu8

Cheers!
Nick
